outcomes: Produce musical scores using music notation and playback software.
Demonstrate understanding of basic concepts of music theory, arrangement, and orchestration relating to music notation.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Create adaptive music for a video game using principles of game audio production.
Integrate adaptive music and interactive mixing into a game utilizing audio middleware.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Perform choral literature, combined with study/travel, to demonstrate an understanding of the role of choral arts in world cultures.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Apply the principles of piano collaboration, as a member of a duo with other instruments or voice, in a live musical performance.
Demonstrate leadership skills in choral accompaniment through conducting, leading & accompanying vocal warm-ups, directing group singing, and coaching beginning instrumentalists and singers.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Evaluate idiomatic and stylistic similarities and differences among the visual and temporal arts.
Translate an artistic response to an experience in visual and performing arts through written critiques.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of workplace skills and professional goals through personal reflection and performance evaluation.
Demonstrate achievement of professional knowledge and career mobility strategies.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate meal planning, costing, and food preparation for an assigned health condition or disease state.
Examine the role of specific foods as they relate to nutrition and wellness.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze and interpret spatial information and data; construct and describe maps, charts and graphs relating to geological, chemical, physical, and biological oceanography.
Solve simple word and numerical problems about oceanography using linear equations and conversion factors.

Explain the major processes that govern ocean-climate interactions, ocean basin formation and evolution, ocean circulation, marine chemistry, beach dynamics, and biological productivity in various zones of the ocean.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Describe the formation of Monterey Bay and the Monterey Submarine Canyon.
Explain the oceanographic processes that control seasonal and long-term variations in the Monterey Bay.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of syntax, semantics, and natural deduction method in sentential and predicate logic producing proofs of argument validity.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze and apply selected ethical theories to contemporary moral issues and respond by producing research-based critical analyses and argumentative essays.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate competency in applied ethics pertaining to the case studies provided.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Recognize and analyze the structure of both deductive and inductive arguments, recognize and evaluate formal and informal fallacies, and produce well-reasoned written and/or oral arguments.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze and evaluate selected theories and issues in Philosophy of Religion and respond by writing research-based critical analyses and argumentative essays.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Investigate physical phenomena experimentally using appropriate equipment and methods, and make valid comparisons with theoretical predictions.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze and solve problems using the concepts, equations and methods of classical mechanics, thermodynamics and waves in both independent and collaborative settings.
Investigate physical phenomena experimentally using appropriate equipment and methods, and make valid comparisons with theoretical predictions.
Clearly communicate results of scientific inquiries in both oral and written form.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes

outcomes: Analyze and solve problems using the concepts, equations, and methods of electricity and magnetism in both independent and collaborative settings.
Investigate physical phenomena experimentally using appropriate equipment and methods, and make valid comparisons with theoretical predictions.
Clearly communicate results of scientific inquiries in both oral and written form.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the structures, interactions, and functioning of the various levels of government in the United States.
Synthesize knowledge and analysis of political events and concepts to construct a personal political viewpoint.
Analyze and assess theoretical arguments, empirical evidence, and political events.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Write critical analytical essays on specific topics in international relations containing a thesis, appropriate historical evidence, and anticipating counter arguments to the proposed thesis.
Synthesize and analyze the major events, theories, and transformations in the history of the modern international system, from the earliest evidence to the present.
Critically analyze primary and historical sources to investigate specific events, topics, or issues in international relations.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Describe basic psychological concepts and theories and explain how biological, environmental, and sociocultural factors influence behavior and mental processes.
Apply psychological principles to assess and change one's life and communities in positive ways.
Use scientific reasoning and empirical evidence to draw conclusions about behavior and mental processes.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Compare and contrast the effects of several personality variables on behavior.
Analyze and evaluate theories of mental processes.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Compare and contrast how biological, environmental, cognitive and other variables contribute to psychological disorders.
Analyze and evaluate theories of mental processes.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Assess the effects of social, psychological, cultural, economic and historical variables on close relationships.
Analyze the interaction of individual psychology and communication in relationships.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Compare and contrast the effects of social and cultural variables on behavior.
Analyze and evaluate theories of mental processes related to social behaviors.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze radiographs of the breast for proper projection, marker placement, exposure factors, artifacts, demonstration of appropriate anatomy and overall image quality.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Identify normal and abnormal human anatomy in any plane on ultrasound, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance images.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze scan parameters appropriate to patient symptomology and pathology.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze sequence parameters appropriate to patient symptomology and pathology.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze acceptable ethical and legal parameters when imaging and caring for patients.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate competency in chest, abdomen, upper and lower extremities radiography on mock patients.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Perform a minimum of five additional competencies as well as demonstrate retention of skills on three other exams previously tested for competency.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Create a diagnostic x-ray image by selecting the best parameters and accessory equipment for most imaging situations.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate laboratory skills competency in upper and lower gastrointestinal tract, urinary, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum radiography on mock patients.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Complete all required competencies to be eligible for the national certification exam and entry into the workforce.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze radiographic exam outcomes for the pediatric patient.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze basic human pathology seen in medical imaging.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Evaluate the dynamics of human social behavior, interaction, and structures using a sociological perspective.
Formulate individual- and societal- level analysis employing sociological theories, concepts, research, and data sources.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Evaluate the dynamics of human social behavior, interaction, and structures related to crime and criminal justice using a sociological perspective.
Formulate individual- and societal- level analysis of crime and criminal justice employing sociological theories, concepts, research, and data sources.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Evaluate the dynamics of human social behavior, interaction, and structures related to contemporary social problems using a sociological perspective.
Formulate individual- and societal- level analysis of contemporary social problems employing sociological theories, concepts, research, and data sources.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Evaluate the dynamics of social identity, interaction, and structure related to Latino/as using social scientific perspectives.
Formulate individual- and societal- level analyses of Latino/as employing social scientific theories, concepts, research, and data sources.

Critically discuss the intersection of race and ethnicity with other forms of difference affected by hierarchy and oppression, such as class, gender, sexuality, religion, spirituality, national origin, immigration status, ability, and/or age.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Understand and apply simple grammatical structures of Spanish in conversations about familiar topics.
Express basic opinions, needs and desires in the present.
Demonstrate a working knowledge of Spanish in simple, uncomplicated transactions.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Interpret orally and in writing a variety of cultural and literary texts in Spanish.
Demonstrate accurate use of orthography, vocabulary, and grammar of standard Spanish in written and oral language.
Demonstrate an increasing knowledge of cultural, historical, and social topics of the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Interpret and analyze a Latin American literary text using appropriate terminology in written and spoken Spanish.
Evaluate in Spanish the ways in which literature portrays and reflects Latin American societies and cultures.
Demonstrate skills to narrate and describe in Spanish using all the major time frames with grammatical correctness.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate improved proficiency in written and oral language, including application of grammar, orthography/spelling, and adaptation of language to various settings and contexts.
Demonstrate knowledge of cultural, historical, and social topics of the Spanish-speaking world.
Analyze and discuss a variety of literary and cultural texts from the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Explain recent changes in Latin American society.
Evaluate the ways in which films represent Latin American society.
Analyze a Latin American film in its historical and social contexts using appropriate terminology in oral and written Spanish.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Analyze and organize a set of data using the techniques of descriptive statistics.
Analyze and develop the meaning of both the confidence interval and hypothesis testing reasoning processes using descriptive statistics and probability.

Evaluate certain inferential statistical problems and decide how to produce estimates of and decisions about certain population parameters using the confidence interval and hypothesis testing reasoning processes.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Select, analyze, and perform selections from dramatic texts demonstrating a comprehensive knowledge of the performance skills of memorization, vocal projection, spatial awareness, stage directions, physical expression and character analysis.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Demonstrate the essentials of collaborative story building in performance of non-scripted theatre in comic and serious genres.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Direct a theatrical piece interpreting its dramatic structure, style, genre, and sociological implications and demonstrating an ability to evoke performances in actors for the stage and for the camera.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Apply stagecraft design and installation principles to create backstage elements for a script.
Organize the crew, materials, tools, and technology required to build or install backstage elements according to production plans safely and efficiently.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Present and defend design solutions.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Investigate various scene painting techniques and methods.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Synthesize musical, dramatic and physical components of musical theater performing through participation in a professional production.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Evaluate personal values, artistic skill sets, and career goals.
Create a plan to succeed in personal artistic career goals by investigating business, technology, and communication tools.
Design, develop, and present a project that envisions a creative career pathway.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Assess how social institutions, public policies, and cultural formations affect the lives of diverse groups of women.
Formulate feminist analyses of the experiences of diverse groups of women using theories, concepts, and research from the field of women's studies.
Analyze prevailing scholarly explanations for systemic gender disparities using an intersectional feminist approach.

rows.heading: Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be prepared to:
outcomes: Assess the historical and contemporary origins of the inequitable social standing of Chicanas/Latinas relative to other social groups.
Analyze the effects of systemic inequalities on the personal identities, lived experiences, and opportunity structures of Chicanas/Latinas.
Appraise Chicana/Latina resilience, agency, and social justice activism in addressing challenges to and struggles of their communities.

Investigate sexism and racism as they relate to class position, documentation status, linguistic difference, sexual orientation, religious background, spiritual practice, national origin, tribal affiliation, age, ability, and other dimensions of human experience.
